title: CNN stages liver fibrosis from non-contrast MRI in rats
summary: A convolutional neural network classified three liver-fibrosis stages from non-contrast T1-weighted MRI in a 99-rat study. The abstract reports stage-specific test AUCs of 0.76, 0.88 and 0.79 after an 80/20 split of one selected image per rat. These animal-model results do not establish human diagnosis; full reference-standard procedures and rat grouping for the separate segmentation evaluation were not available in the abstract.
ai_technology: nnU-Net segmentation and convolutional neural network classification
organization: Qingdao University; The Affiliated Hospital of Qingdao University

evidence.tested: 99 male Wistar rats and2628 MRI slices. The abstract describes a70/30 image split for segmentation (test Dice0.8477), and one maximum-diameter image per rat with80/20 stage-stratified image selection for classification. Reported class accuracies0.73/0.89/0.84 and AUCs0.76/0.88/0.79.
evidence.unknown: Primary abstract and indexed publisher excerpts only; no full article/supplement retrieved. Exact histologic reference/rater protocol and segmentation grouping by rat remain unverified; slice-level splitting may inflate segmentation results. Prospective animal acquisition does not establish prospective frozen-model performance or human transfer.
evidence.ai_role: nnU-Net delineates liver regions and a CNN learns MRI features to classify no, early or progressive liver fibrosis in the induced rat model.

source_review.scope: Primary PubMed XML complete abstract, publication history and author affiliations; corroborating publisher-indexed excerpts retained by researcher. Full publisher article unavailable; no full Methods claim.
